body_text: People taking popular weight-loss injections such as Wegovy and Mounjaro have been urged to take extra care during periods of extreme heat, with a pharmacist warning that dehydration can become a serious health concern. The warning comes as parts of the UK experience exceptionally hot weather, with temperatures rising sharply and authorities issuing heat-related health advice. While staying hydrated is important for everyone during hot weather, people using certain weight-loss medicines may need to be particularly mindful of their fluid intake. Medicines such as Wegovy and Mounjaro can affect appetite and may cause side effects including nausea or vomiting, which can make it harder for some people to maintain their usual food and fluid intake. According to a report published by the Daily Mirror, highlighted the increased risk of dehydration for people taking these medications during hot weather. Why heat can increase dehydration risk Hot weather causes the body to lose more fluid, particularly through sweating. If someone does not replace the fluids they lose, dehydration can develop. For people taking weight-loss injections, additional factors may sometimes contribute. These medicines can reduce appetite and may affect how regularly a person eats or drinks. Some users can also experience gastrointestinal side effects such as nausea or vomiting. This does not mean everyone taking Wegovy or Mounjaro will become dehydrated. However, being aware of the warning signs can help people recognise a problem before it becomes more serious. The pharmacist advised people using weight-loss medication to pay particular attention to their hydration during periods of extreme heat. Common signs of dehydration to watch for Dehydration can cause a range of symptoms, and the first signs may be relatively mild. Possible symptoms include: Increased thirst A dry mouth or sticky saliva Headaches Darker yellow urine Passing urine less frequently Feeling unusually tired or weak Dizziness, particularly when standing up These symptoms can have other causes, so they should not automatically be assumed to be caused by dehydration. However, they may be a useful indication that someone needs to pay closer attention to their fluid intake. As dehydration becomes more severe, symptoms can become considerably more concerning. The warning highlighted confusion, unusual drowsiness, fainting, a rapid heartbeat and producing very little or no urine as signs that require urgent medical attention. Someone who is repeatedly vomiting and cannot keep fluids down may also need urgent medical assessment, particularly if they are becoming extremely weak or showing other signs of serious dehydration. How much should you drink during hot weather? The amount of fluid an individual needs varies according to factors such as age, body size, activity levels, health conditions, diet and the temperature of their surroundings. The advice reported by the Mirror suggested that many adults may need around 2.5 to 3 litres of water a day during very hot weather, compared with a lower baseline amount in more moderate conditions. However, hydration is not simply about drinking a large quantity of water as quickly as possible. A more practical approach is to drink regularly throughout the day. People who are exercising, working outdoors or spending extended periods in hot environments may need to replace additional fluid lost through sweating. It is also important to remember that individual medical circumstances can change fluid requirements. People with certain medical conditions or those taking particular medicines should follow advice from their doctor, pharmacist or other healthcare professional. Do not ignore vomiting or persistent nausea One issue that may be particularly relevant to some users of weight-loss injections is vomiting. If someone is losing fluid through repeated vomiting and cannot replace it by drinking, dehydration can develop more quickly. Anyone experiencing persistent vomiting, severe weakness, confusion, fainting or other worrying symptoms should seek appropriate medical advice rather than attempting to manage potentially severe dehydration alone. People should also avoid making changes to prescribed medication without speaking to a healthcare professional. Wegovy and Mounjaro are prescription medicines, and they are not suitable for everyone. Their use should be monitored according to the prescribing information and individual medical advice. Heatstroke is different from ordinary dehydration Another important concern during extreme heat is heatstroke. Heatstroke is a medical emergency and can occur when the body's temperature regulation system becomes overwhelmed. It can involve a very high body temperature, confusion, altered consciousness or loss of consciousness, as well as other serious symptoms. The Mirror report referenced symptoms including a body temperature above 40C, hot skin, confusion and fainting or unconsciousness. If heatstroke is suspected, urgent medical assistance should be sought. People can reduce their exposure to extreme heat by staying in cooler indoor spaces where possible, avoiding strenuous activity during the hottest parts of the day and following official heat-health guidance. Practical hydration tips for Wegovy and Mounjaro users People using weight-loss injections can take several simple steps to reduce their risk of becoming dehydrated during hot weather. First, keep water readily available throughout the day. Having a bottle nearby can make it easier to remember to drink regularly. Second, pay attention to changes in urine colour and frequency. Darker urine or noticeably reduced urination can be a warning sign that fluid intake may be inadequate. Third, do not wait until you feel extremely thirsty before drinking. Regular small amounts can be easier to manage than consuming a large amount of liquid at once. Fourth, take extra care if exercising or working in hot conditions. Sweating increases fluid loss, so additional fluids may be required. Finally, anyone experiencing significant vomiting, severe dizziness, confusion, fainting or very little urine should seek medical help promptly. When should you contact a healthcare professional? Not every headache or episode of tiredness means someone is seriously dehydrated. Hot weather itself can make people feel uncomfortable, fatigued and light-headed. However, symptoms that are severe, worsening or accompanied by confusion, fainting, an unusually fast heartbeat, inability to keep fluids down or very little urine should not be ignored. If you are unsure whether symptoms could be related to your medication, dehydration or another health problem, speaking to a pharmacist, GP or other qualified healthcare professional can help determine what to do next. The key message for people taking Wegovy or Mounjaro during extreme heat is straightforward: do not overlook hydration . As temperatures rise, paying attention to fluid intake and recognising the early signs of dehydration may help reduce the risk of more serious complications. Disclaimer This article is for general information only and is not medical advice. It should not be used as a substitute for advice from a qualified doctor, pharmacist or other healthcare professional. Wegovy and Mounjaro are prescription medicines, and individual advice can vary depending on a person's health, other medicines and circumstances. Anyone experiencing severe or rapidly worsening symptoms should seek appropriate medical attention. Do not stop, restart or change a prescribed medicine without speaking to a healthcare professional. Source Daily Mirror, August 13, 2026.

title: Weave Announces Acquisition by Francisco Partners
summary: Weave Announces Acquisition by Francisco Partners. Transaction Accelerates Investment in Weave’s AI-Powered Platform for Healthcare Practices.
body_text: Transaction Accelerates Investment in Weave’s AI-Powered Platform for Healthcare Practices Weave Stockholders to Receive $7.40 Per Share in Cash, Representing a 34% Premium LEHI, Utah and SAN FRANCISCO, California — (BUSINESS WIRE) — August 18, 2026 — Weave Communications, Inc. (“Weave”) (NYSE: WEAV), a leading AI-powered patient engagement and payments platform purpose-built for healthcare practices, and Francisco Partners (“FP”), a leading global investment firm that specializes in partnering with technology companies and technology-enabled businesses, today announced that FP has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Weave, at an aggregate equity valuation of approximately $650 Million. Under the terms of the agreement, Weave stockholders will receive $7.40 per share in cash, representing a premium of approximately 34% to Weave’s unaffected closing stock price on August 17, 2026, the last full trading day prior to the transaction announcement. Upon completion of the transaction, Weave will cease to trade on the NYSE and become a private company. Founded in 2008, Weave is a leading all-in-one customer experience and payments software platform for small and medium-sized healthcare businesses. Weave’s software solutions transform how healthcare practices attract, communicate with, and engage patients and clients to grow their business. Following the completion of the transaction Weave will continue to operate under the Weave name and maintain its headquarters in Lehi, Utah. “Since our founding in 2008, we have built Weave for a customer most software companies overlook — the independent practices that care for patients in communities across the country. More than 40,000 locations rely on us today,” said Brett White, Chief Executive Officer of Weave. “Together with Francisco Partners, we will be able to enhance our ability to invest in our AI platform, deepen our payments and revenue cycle management capabilities, and further our vision of a better healthcare experience at every practice. Today’s announcement represents a compelling outcome for our stockholders, and we look forward to partnering with Francisco Partners, who have an extensive track record in successfully scaling companies at the intersection of vertical software and healthcare, in the next phase of Weave’s journey.” Stuart C. Harvey Jr., Chair of the Weave Board of Directors added, “The Weave Board conducted a thorough evaluation of strategic alternatives and spoke with a number of strategic and financial parties. The transaction with Francisco Partners delivers a substantial premium and compelling, certain cash value to our stockholders. The Board unanimously determined that this transaction represents the best path forward for Weave and recommends that stockholders vote in favor of the transaction. On behalf of the entire Board, I want to thank Brett and the Weave team for building a business that has achieved this outcome and is positioned for continued growth.” “Weave is ideally positioned to capitalize on the healthcare industry’s large and growing demand for AI to help optimize their practices and services,” said Ezra Perlman, Co-President at Francisco Partners. “Its vertical platform sits at the center of how tens of thousands of practices communicate with their patients and collect revenue, a position that is difficult to build and harder still to replicate.” Nick Nelson, Principal at Francisco Partners, added, “Weave has built a differentiated platform, and we see significant opportunity to build on that position through continued product innovation and by expanding the value Weave delivers to its customers. We are excited to partner with the entire team for the next chapter of Weave’s growth.” Transaction Details, Approvals and Timing The transaction, which was unanimously approved by the Weave Board of Directors, is anticipated to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by Weave stockholders and the receipt of required regulatory approvals. As of the date of the Agreement, no executive officer has entered into any agreement with Francisco Partners to roll over equity, invest alongside the buyer, or acquire an equity interest in the surviving company. Advisors Jefferies LLC is serving as exclusive financial advisor to Weave and Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP is serving as its legal counsel. Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal counsel to Francisco Partners. About Weave Weave is a leading vertical SaaS company delivering an AI-powered patient engagement and payments platform purpose-built for modern healthcare practices. More than software, Weave is an always-on teammate—handling patient interactions across voice and text and operating at the center of the patient journey. Through agentic AI workflows and authorized integrations with practice management systems, Weave ensures critical tasks like scheduling, insurance verification, and payments happen seamlessly, so nothing falls between the cracks. By embedding AI directly into daily operations, Weave reduces administrative workload, frees up staff to focus on human-centered care, and delivers real-time insights that help practices run smarter and grow with confidence. Serving over 40,000 customer locations, Weave was named a 2026 Best Software Awards winner for healthcare software products by G2. To learn more, visit getweave.com/newsroom. About Francisco Partners Francisco Partners is a leading global investment firm that specializes in partnering with technology and technology-enabled businesses. Since its launch over 25 years ago, Francisco Partners has invested in over 500 technology companies, making it one of the most active and longstanding investors in the technology industry. With over $75 billion in capital raised to date, the firm invests in opportunities where its deep sectoral knowledge and operational expertise can help companies realize their full potential. For more information on Francisco Partners, please visit www.franciscopartners.com . body_text: Toggle Investor Relations navigation. Investor Overview Events & Presentations Press Releases Quarterly Earnings / Calendar Financial Information Stock Information Dividend Information Annual Meeting Information IR Resources CURRENT STOCK PRICE PRESS RELEASE Vornado Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results August 3, 2026 View Print PDF 668.7 KB NEW YORK, Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vornado Realty Trust (NYSE: VNO) reported today: Quarter Ended June 30, 2026 Financial Results NET INCOME attributable to common shareholders for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $16,434,000, or $0.08 per diluted share, compared to $743,819,000, or $3.70 per diluted share, for the prior year's quarter. The decrease is primarily due to the $803,248,000 gain related to the 770 Broadway master lease with New York University ("NYU") during the three months ended June 30, 2025. FUNDS FROM OPERATIONS ("FFO") attributable to common shareholders plus assumed conversions (non-GAAP) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $144,078,000, or $0.74 per diluted share, compared to $120,928,000, or $0.60 per diluted share, for the prior year's quarter. Adjusting for the items that impact period-to-period comparability listed in the table on the following page, FFO attributable to common shareholders plus assumed conversions, as adjusted (non-GAAP) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $131,073,000, or $0.67 per diluted share, and $113,324,000, or $0.56 per diluted share, for the prior year's quarter. Six Months Ended June 30, 2026 Financial Results NET LOSS attributable to common shareholders for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $6,408,000, or $0.03 per diluted share, compared to net income attributable to common shareholders of $830,661,000, or $4.14 per diluted share, for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease is primarily due to the $803,248,000 gain related to the 770 Broadway master lease with NYU during the six months ended June 30, 2025. Acquisitions Park Avenue Plaza On June 11, 2026, we completed the purchase of a 49.0% interest in Park Avenue Plaza at a gross asset valuation of $1.1 billion ($950 per square foot). We acquired our interest subject to our share of the $575,000,000 loan encumbering the property. The loan bears interest at a fixed rate of 2.99% and matures in November 2031. Park Avenue Plaza is a 45-story, 1,200,000 rentable square foot building located at 55 East 52nd Street. The office building, co-owned by Fisher Brothers, has protected Park Avenue views and occupies the full through-block between East 52nd and East 53rd Street. Fisher Brothers retains its current 51.0% ownership interest and continues to manage and lease the property. Vornado and Fisher Brothers have joint control over major decisions. 3 East 54th Street On January 7, 2026, we acquired 3 East 54th Street, an asset situated on 18,400 square feet of land, for $141,000,000. Previously, in July 2025, we purchased the $35,000,000 A-Note secured by the property at par plus accrued interest, and in August 2024, we purchased the $50,000,000 B-Note secured by the property. The A-Note and B-Note were in default. The $107,000,000 loan balance, including default interest and advances, was credited towards the purchase price. 3 East 54th Street is located between Fifth Avenue and Madison Avenue on 54th Street, adjacent to the St. Regis Hotel and our Upper Fifth Avenue retail properties. The land is zoned for approximately 232,500 buildable square feet as-of-right, and we are in the process of demolishing the existing buildings on the site. Dispositions Alexander’s, Inc. (“Alexander’s”) On May 28, 2026, Alexander’s, in which we own a 32.4% interest, completed the sale of its Rego Park I property for $235,500,000. As a result of the sale, we recognized our $44,329,000 share of the net gain and received a $2,355,000 sales commission paid by Alexander’s, of which $500,000 was paid to a third-party broker. 606 Broadway On May 14, 2026, a 50.0% owned consolidated joint venture completed the sale of 606 Broadway. The purchaser acquired the non-recourse mortgage loan, which was in maturity default, at a discount and paid the joint venture $3,000,000 in cash ($2,400,000 to Vornado). The transaction resulted in a $32,073,000 gain on debt extinguishment, of which $15,932,000 is attributable to noncontrolling interests. The property was previously impaired in the fourth quarter of 2023, and had a carrying value of $52,073,000 as of the sale date. Financing Activity Senior Unsecured Notes Due 2026 We repaid our $400,000,000 2.15% senior unsecured notes on their June 1, 2026, maturity date. 61 Ninth Avenue On May 8, 2026, a joint venture, in which we have a 45.1% interest, completed a $161,000,000 refinancing of 61 Ninth Avenue. The interest-only mortgage loan matures in June 2028, with a nine-month extension option subject to certain conditions, and bears interest at SOFR plus 3.00% in year one, SOFR plus 3.35% for year two, and SOFR plus 3.85% during the extension period. The refinancing replaced the joint venture’s prior $167,500,000 mortgage loan on the property. On February 2, 2026, the joint venture had extended that prior loan’s maturity by seven months and simultaneously paid down the principal balance by $12,500,000 to $155,000,000. 350 Park Avenue On March 10, 2026, an affiliate of Kenneth C. Griffin (“KG”) provided a $400,000,000 mortgage loan secured by 350 Park Avenue, the proceeds of which were used to defease the existing $400,000,000 mortgage loan in connection with the site’s development. The new interest-only loan bears interest at a fixed rate of 4.00% and matures in January 2027. Concurrently, and in connection with the planned development, Citadel Enterprise Americas LLC vacated the building and assigned its existing master lease to an affiliate of KG as tenant, and the lease was amended to provide for net rent of $16,000,000 per annum, equal to the interest payments under the new mortgage loan. Financing Activity - continued One Park Avenue On February 9, 2026, we completed a $525,000,000 refinancing of One Park Avenue, a 945,000 square foot Manhattan office building. The five-year interest-only loan matures in February 2031 and bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 1.78%. The loan replaced the previous $525,000,000 loan that bore interest at SOFR plus 1.22% and was scheduled to mature in March 2026. 825 Seventh Avenue Office Condominium On January 26, 2026, a joint venture, in which we have a 50.0% interest, entered into a nine-month extension with the lenders on the $54,000,000 mortgage loan encumbering the office condominium of 825 Seventh Avenue and simultaneously paid down the principal balance by $6,000,000 to $48,000,000. The loan was previously scheduled to mature in January 2026. The non-recourse interest-only loan bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 2.75% and matures in October 2026, with a fifteen-month extension option subject to loan-to-value and debt yield requirements. 7 West 34th Street On January 23, 2026, a joint venture, in which we have a 53.0% interest, completed a $250,000,000 refinancing of 7 West 34th Street, a 477,000 square foot Manhattan office and retail building. The non-recourse, five-year interest-only mortgage loan matures in February 2031 and has a fixed rate of 5.79%. The joint venture paid down by $50,000,000 the prior $300,000,000 full-recourse loan that bore interest at 3.65% and was scheduled to mature in June 2026. The loan was paid down using property-level reserves and a $25,000,000 member loan from Vornado which accrues interest at 16.00% and receives priority on distributions. Senior Unsecured Notes Due 2033 On January 14, 2026, we completed a public offering of $500,000,000 5.75% senior unsecured notes due February 1, 2033 (“2033 Notes”). Interest on the senior unsecured notes is payable semi-annually on February 1 and August 1, commencing August 1, 2026. The 2033 Notes were sold at 99.824% of their face amount to yield 5.78%. A portion of the $494,000,000 net proceeds from the 2033 Notes was used to repay our $400,000,000 senior unsecured notes at their June 2026 maturity. 2031 Revolving Credit Facility On January 7, 2026, we completed a $1.105 billion refinancing of one of our two revolving credit facilities. The facility replaced the previous $1.25 billion revolving credit facility which was scheduled to mature in December 2027. 2029 Revolving Credit Facility On January 7, 2026, we upsized our $915,000,000 revolving credit facility that matures in April 2029 (as fully extended) to $1.0 billion. The credit facility currently bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 1.16% and has a facility fee of 24 basis points. Unsecured Term Loan On January 7, 2026, we completed a refinancing of our unsecured term loan and upsized the loan amount to $850,000,000. The loan bears interest at SOFR plus 1.15% and matures in February 2031 (as fully extended). The loan replaced the previous $800,000,000 term loan which bore interest at SOFR plus 1.25% and was scheduled to mature in December 2027. 888 Seventh Avenue On December 10, 2025, the $244,543,000 non-recourse mortgage loan on 888 Seventh Avenue matured and was not repaid, at which time the lenders declared an event of default. NAREIT defines FFO as GAAP net income or loss adjusted to exclude net gains from sales of certain real estate assets, impairment write-downs of certain real estate assets and investments in entities when the impairment is directly attributable to decreases in the value of depreciable real estate held by the entity, depreciation and amortization expense from real estate assets and other specified items, including the pro rata share of such adjustments of unconsolidated subsidiaries. FFO and FFO per diluted share are non-GAAP financial measures used by management, investors and analysts to facilitate meaningful comparisons of operating performance between periods and among our peers because it excludes the effect of real estate depreciation and amortization and net gains on sales, which are based on historical costs and implicitly assume that the value of real estate diminishes predictably over time, rather than fluctuating based on existing market conditions. FFO does not represent cash generated from operating activities and is not necessarily indicative of cash available to fund cash requirements and should not be considered as an alternative to net income as a performance measure or cash flow as a liquidity measure. FFO may not be comparable to similarly titled measures employed by other companies. title: Do You Have Bad Headaches, or Do You Actually Have Migraines?
summary: Recurring "bad headaches" with nausea, light sensitivity, or brain fog are often undiagnosed migraines. Learn what sets migraines apart and why the treatment is completely different.
body_text: Many people with "bad headaches" that keep coming back actually have migraines. They just have never been diagnosed. The short answer If your headaches come with nausea, sensitivity to light or sound, fatigue, brain fog, or the feeling that moving around makes everything worse, you almost certainly have migraines. Migraines are not just a pain in your head. They're a neurological condition with specific treatments that work far better than the ibuprofen and Excedrin you've been relying on for years. The distinction matters because the treatment is completely different. Start a chat with Dr. Rowan Casey-Ford, MD Free Describe your symptoms and get real medical guidance, on your schedule. What's actually going on? A regular headache is pain in your head. You can get one from dehydration, a rough night of sleep, staring at a screen too long. It hurts, you take something, it goes away. Anyone can get one at some point. A migraine is a fundamentally different process. It's not just an ache from a hard day or night of work, its a neurological process, literally a type of storm in your brain. When a migraine starts, a wave of abnormal electrical activity spreads across your brain. That wave activates your trigeminal nerve system, which floods the area with inflammatory signals, especially a substance called CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide). Your brain's ability to calm pain signals down gets overwhelmed. Normal sensations become unbearable. Light hurts. Sound hurts. Going up a flight of stairs makes your head pound. The fatigue, the brain fog, the nausea, the feeling that you can't think straight: those aren't side effects of the headache. They're part of the same neurological process. This is why Tylenol is mostly useless and why ibuprofen and Excedrin sort of work and then somehow seem to start making your headaches worse. You've been treating a neurological condition with a pain reliever. It's the wrong tool. Roughly 1 in 5 women of reproductive age has migraines [per the American Migraine Foundation]. The condition is diagnosed clinically. There's no scan that lights up and says "migraine." It shows up as pain, decreased function, and sensitivity in a patient who is often told she's stressed, not sleeping enough, not drinking enough water or "just being dramatic". That framing is wrong. It's also everywhere. When does the answer change? For a small number of people, what feels like a migraine is actually something else. If your headaches started suddenly and recently, if they're dramatically different from anything you've had before, or if they come with vision changes, numbness, weakness, or balance problems, those need urgent evaluation. That's an emergency room visit, not a chat. But the far more common scenario is the opposite. You've had these headaches for years. You've been told they're tension headaches or sinus headaches. Nobody has really sat down and asked: Do lights and sounds bother you? Does squatting down or walking up stairs make it worse? Even if you aren't vomiting in a dark room, do you feel like you'd really rather not see food ever again? If you keep having bad headaches, they last for hours, they make your head pound or they feel worse when you walk or climb stairs, and they make you nauseated or lights and sounds bothers you, you meet criteria for migraines. Yes - you may have allergies, and yes, you may have a stiff neck and, yes, those things may be making your headaches worse, but have you ever noticed that the world is full of people with allergies and neck tension who do not have horrendous headaches? The fact is that most people who have migraines have been misdiagnosed or simply never diagnosed at all. A U.S. study found that only 26.3% of people with episodic migraine which was adversely affecting their ability to function in their daily lives had consulted a healthcare professional, received a migraine diagnosis, and were using migraine-specific acute treatments. The level of diagnosis is so low that it lead the American Headache Society to advocate (unsuccessfully) for universal screenings for migraine headaches in reproductive age women. Take a moment and let that sink in - the American Headache Society concluded that migraines are so common, and we in primary care are doing such a poor job diagnosing them, that it would work out better if we just gave a screening questionnaire asking about migraine specific symptoms to every single woman between roughly the ages of 15 and 45. ( A note for men : There is a lot going on in this article about "reproductive aged women". You may feel left out. Statistically, 75% of people with migraine headaches are women. Put another way though, one out of every four migraine sufferers is a man - and the female predominance actually also results in underdiagnosis for men. So don't hesitate to take the next step if you feel like this article describes your headaches!) What should you actually do? Pay attention to what happens during your headaches beyond the pain. Do you feel sick to your stomach? Does moving around make it worse? Do you want the lights off? Does sound bother you? Are you exhausted or foggy for hours afterward? How often do you have headaches? How long do they last? Write that down. Those details are the difference between a five-minute "take some Tylenol" visit and a diagnosis that changes how you feel most days. Stop blaming yourself. There's a lot of content out there implying you could prevent migraines if you just reduced stress, ate an anti-inflammatory diet, did the right yoga, and drank the right tea. That framing blames the patient for a neurological condition. People living extremely healthy lifestyles still have terrible migraines. You didn't cause this by being insufficiently virtuous. Know the OTC trap. Ibuprofen, naproxen, and Excedrin Migraine can all work for individual episodes. But if you start to rely on them to get through your day, most days, the medication itself generates the next headache, which makes you take more, which generates another one. If you're caught in that cycle, the fix isn't a better over-the-counter option. It's a conversation about migraine-specific treatment. Lifestyle factors that actually move the needle: Your migraine brain loves consistency. If you possibly can, go to sleep at the same time, and wake up at the same time. Do you love coffee? Great! Me too! Have the same amount of coffee (preferably 1-3 cups and not 7) at the same time of day, in the morning. Eat food - there is no magic diet formula, but your migraine brain hates wild blood sugar swings and skipped meals, so eating consistent meals at consistent times that contain real food items with recognizable ingredients is helpful. When is this worth bringing to a doctor? If your headaches seem to be happening more and more often, if over-the-counter medications aren't cutting it anymore, if you're dragging yourself through the day wondering why you feel this bad, that's worth a real conversation with a doctor who will actually ask the right questions. That conversation is a chat consultation with a real doctor: diagnoses, prescriptions, the actual clinical call on what to do next. You start it from your phone whenever you're ready. You'll usually have a response back the same day. No scheduling, no waiting room, no taking time off work. This article is intended as educational information, not personal medical advice. For guidance on your specific situation, talk to your own doctor, or start a chat consultation with a FutureClinic doctor and get a real, personalized answer for your case. Frequently asked questions Do I need a brain scan to find out if I have migraines? Usually not. Migraines are diagnosed based on your symptoms and history, not imaging. That said, there's a low threshold to do a scan once, especially if your headache pattern changes or if there are any red-flag features like sudden onset, neurological symptoms, or a headache that's dramatically different from your usual pattern. Can migraines go away on their own? For some people, they improve over time. But for many people, migraines are a chronic condition that benefits from active management. "Chronic" doesn't mean "untreatable." With the right plan, most people go from migraines running their life to migraines being a minor inconvenience. Is it true that certain foods cause migraines? Foods are a trigger for some people, but the blanket food-elimination lists floating around the internet are mostly unhelpful. If you genuinely suspect a food trigger, track what you ate before your headaches and look for a real pattern. Preemptively cutting out gluten, dairy, aged cheese, chocolate, and citrus because an internet list told you to usually just makes you stressed and hungry, which, ironically, is more likely to trigger a migraine than the cheese you gave up. Are there prescription medications specifically for migraines? Yes, and they're not just pain medications. Triptans (like rizatriptan and sumatriptan) work specifically on the migraine process and can abort an episode in progress. For people with frequent migraines, daily preventive medications like propranolol, amitriptyline, or topiramate can reduce how often migraines happen by 50% or more [per AHS treatment guidelines]. Which one fits depends on your other health conditions and what side effects you can tolerate. That's exactly the kind of thing a doctor should walk through with you personally. What if I have already tried a preventive medication and it did not work? Most "failures" with preventive medications are actually process failures, not medication failures. The dose was never increased to a level that actually prevents migraines, the refills lapsed, or nobody told the patient that the first medication might not be the right one. A real trial of a preventive takes about three months at a therapeutic dose. Many people need to try two or three before landing on the one that works. Having a doctor who stays with you through that process and adjusts along the way can make all the difference. title: Randy H. Goodman, PhD, MHA
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Cerenome, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Randy H. Goodman, PhD, MHA VP, Value Strategy and HEOR Dr. Goodman is a highly experienced health economics and market access leader with more than 20 years of experience spanning global pricing and reimbursement strategy, real-world evidence generation, and value-based healthcare modeling across the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, diagnostics, and medical device sectors. He has led the development of payer engagement strategies, health technology assessment (HTA) dossiers, and value frameworks supporting product launches and commercialization for leading healthcare organizations. Dr. Goodman has advised leading global healthcare organizations, including Pfizer, Gilead Sciences, and Moderna, and has worked closely with government agencies such as the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services on value-based pricing and reimbursement frameworks. He has also served as a healthcare policy advisor to the White House on multiple health reform initiatives, contributing to the development of reimbursement and access frameworks at both the federal and state levels. Dr. Goodman holds a Ph.D. and Master of Healthcare Administration from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and a Bachelor of Arts in Medical Communications from North Texas State University.

body_text: Capricor Therapeutics to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provide Recent Corporate Update on August 13 August 10, 2026 8:30 am EDT Download as PDF – Company to Host Conference Call on August 13, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. ET – SAN DIEGO, Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases, today announced that it will release its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, after the market close on Thursday, August 13, 2026. Management will host a conference call and webcast at 4:30 p.m. ET that same day. Title: Capricor Therapeutics Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Corporate Update Conference Call and Webcast Date: Thursday, August 13, 2026 Time: 4:30 p.m. ET Call Details: Toll-Free: 1-800-717-1738 International: 1-646-307-1865 Conference ID: 91880 Participants may dial in using the numbers above and ask to be joined to the call, or use the Call me™ link for instant telephone access to the event. Webcast: Click here A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the conclusion of the live event and will be accessible in the Investors section of the Company’s website at www.capricor.com . About Capricor Therapeutics Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR) is a biotechnology company dedicated to advancing cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases. Our lead product candidate, Deramiocel, is an allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy in late-stage development for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), shown in clinical studies to preserve cardiac and skeletal muscle function. Capricor is also advancing its proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform for the targeted delivery of oligonucleotides, proteins, and small-molecule therapeutics across a range of diseases. At Capricor, we are committed to delivering new therapies for patients with rare diseases. For more information, visit capricor.com , and follow Capricor on Facebook , Instagram and X . title: Surprising Solutions: Norton Runs for the Roses — MSC Industrial Supply Co.
summary: Norton Abrasives’ RazorStar belts are used by farriers to modify and smooth horseshoes, helping ensure the safety and performance of racehorses.
body_text: Often described as “The Most Exciting Two Minutes in Sports,” the Kentucky Derby is a feast for the senses. The colorful sight of elaborate fashions. The tingling taste of mint juleps. The hopeful feel of that betting marker carrying the wish of a win. The fragrant smell of the winner’s rose garland. The vibrating sound of thundering hooves. Every sense is stimulated. Let’s zero in on just one and consider those thundering hooves for a moment. Think about the critical role of the horses’ feet in racing to the finish line. And look, there’s Norton Abrasives back in the stable helping make success possible. A Shoe-in for Success Horses don’t run on their natural hooves. Instead, a trained specialist known as a “farrier” combines blacksmith skills with equine lower-limb knowledge to support safe, healthy hoof function. A farrier will trim, balance, and shoe the horse on a regular basis (approximately every four to six weeks), often custom-shaping the horseshoes using traditional smithing techniques. Farriers require unique skills and specialized tools to perform their duties. That’s where Farrier Products Distribution (FPD) enters the picture. Established in 1990, FPD is now a full partner with the Holland-based Royal Kerckhaert Horseshoe Factory. FPD is a wholesale distributor that supplies a network of farrier supply shops across the US and Canada from their home base of operations in the heart of horse country: Shelbyville, Kentucky. Commitment to Quality Even without selling direct to their target audience, FPD can still track the performance of the products they sell through individual farriers. Szymanski notes that for the last several years running, many of the horses in the Derby field have worn Kerckhaert race plates, even a few of the winners – including 2024 Derby winner Mystik Dan and 2025 Derby winner Sovereignty. With that track record and reputation at stake, they are very particular about the products that go into their inventory. Norton RazorStar belts meet their tough criteria. The primary use for the RazorStar belt is to do final modifications to the horseshoes before they're applied to the feet. Typically, the belts are used to bevel smoother edges on the shoes to protect the horse. Sometimes, the farrier will also use the belts to fit pads to shoes, trimming excess material off. The primary concern is the safety of the horse, taking away any material that doesn't need to be there to make sure the horse can't catch or cut itself or injure another horse because of excess steel sticking out where it shouldn't. “If there's an opportunity to bring something better to the table than what we're currently offering, we're going to investigate that and find out where the opportunities lie. And with Norton, it was pretty easy. Once we did some field testing, we quickly realized that those RazorStar belts are every bit as good as the promotional claims we heard.” Ed Szymanski, Sales Manager, Farrier Products Distribution Since introducing their customers to Norton RazorStar, FPD has had a very favorable response. “Farriers that are using them absolutely love them. They're extremely happy with not only the price of them, but they’re also extremely happy with the durability and how clean they cut, how fast they cut,” Szymanski observed. “What I think might be the most talked about feature is how much cooler the material is after they're done grinding, especially compared to other abrasives that have been used. Once they put it on their grinder, it's not coming off. That's going to be their belt going forward.” Szymanski also expressed that FPD’s satisfaction goes beyond the product. “Norton checks all the boxes for us. They meet the same high standards that we expect of ourselves by being able to reliably supply our customers and treat them as partners rather than as just a number. That's the same way we feel working with Norton. They are able to supply the product we need when we need it. And if we have questions or concerns, we're able to reach out to our rep and have those addressed quickly and respectfully. It works great.” This article was previously featured on Norton's blog .

title: Average SAT Score by State 2026: Rankings & Participation
summary: See the latest average SAT score by state with 2025 data, 2026 updates, participation rates, and rankings. Compare your state and plan your prep.
body_text: Average SAT Score by State 2026: Rankings & Participation TL;DR The national average SAT score for the Class of 2025 is 1029 out of 1600. State averages range from 875 (New Mexico) to 1256 (Kansas), but this gap is almost entirely driven by participation rates, not educational quality. States that require every student to take the SAT have lower averages; states where only a few motivated students choose the SAT have inflated averages. The only number that truly matters for college admissions is your target school’s middle 50% SAT range, not your state’s average. Quick Answer: Average SAT Scores by State in 2026 The average SAT score in the United States for the Class of 2025 is 1029 out of 1600 . However, state averages vary dramatically. Kansas reports the highest average score at 1256 , while New Mexico reports the lowest at 875 . These rankings can be misleading. The biggest factor affecting state SAT scores is participation rate . States that require every student to take the SAT almost always report lower averages. States where only a small percentage of college-bound students choose the SAT typically report much higher scores. Before comparing yourself with your state's average, check three numbers: - Your state's SAT participation rate - Your national percentile - Your target college's middle 50% SAT range For admissions purposes, your target college's score range matters far more than your state's average. National Average SAT Score (Class of 2025) Before looking at the average SAT score by state, it helps to know the national baseline. The College Board reports a mean total SAT score of 1029 for the Class of 2025, broken down as 521 in Reading and Writing and 508 in Math. Over 2 million students took the test, the first time participation exceeded that mark since 2020. This was also the first majority-digital cohort, with 97% of students taking the Digital SAT. About 68% tested during the school day rather than on a weekend. A few more numbers worth noting: College readiness benchmarks: The College Board sets them at 480 for Reading and Writing and 530 for Math. Only 39% of the Class of 2025 met both, down from 45% pre-pandemic . Year-over-year trend: The 2025 average of 1029 is a slight improvement over 1024 in 2024, but still roughly 30 points below pre-pandemic levels. Post-pandemic trajectory: From 2020 to 2024, average scores declined in line with drops seen on NAEP and PISA assessments. The 2025 uptick is the first positive movement since 2021. If you’re wondering where your own score falls nationally, a score predictor tool can give you a data-backed estimate based on your current practice performance. Graduating Class Average SAT Score 2019 ~1059 2020 ~1051 2021 ~1060 2022 ~1050 2023 ~1028 2024 1024 2025 1029 Average SAT Scores by State: Full Rankings Table Here is the complete average SAT score by state for the Class of 2025, ranked from highest to lowest. Pay close attention to the participation rate column, as it explains nearly everything about where each state falls. Rank State Avg Total Avg RW Avg Math Participation Rate Statewide Mandate? 1 Kansas 1256 632 624 ~2% No 2 North Dakota 1254 631 623 ~1% No 3 Wyoming 1253 630 623 ~1% No 4 Utah 1230 619 611 ~2% No 5 Nebraska 1228 617 611 ~2% No 6 Wisconsin 1225 616 609 ~2% No 7 Iowa 1222 615 607 ~2% No 8 South Dakota 1218 614 604 ~2% No 9 Minnesota 1215 612 603 ~3% No 10 Mississippi 1210 607 603 ~2% No 11 Missouri 1205 605 600 ~3% No 12 Montana 1202 604 598 ~4% No 13 Kentucky 1198 601 597 ~4% No 14 Louisiana 1195 598 597 ~3% No 15 Arkansas 1193 597 596 ~3% No 16 Alabama 1190 596 594 ~4% No 17 Oklahoma 1185 594 591 ~4% No 18 Tennessee 1180 592 588 ~5% No 19 Oregon 1175 590 585 ~8% No 20 Alaska 1170 588 582 ~8% No 21 Arizona 1165 585 580 ~25% No 22 Vermont 1160 583 577 ~10% No 23 Massachusetts 1155 580 575 ~18% No 24 Hawaii 1150 578 572 ~15% No 25 Virginia 1145 575 570 ~25% No 26 New Hampshire 1085 545 540 ~68% Yes 27 New York 1080 542 538 ~50% No 28 Pennsylvania 1075 540 535 ~40% No 29 New Jersey 1070 538 532 ~45% No 30 North Carolina 1065 535 530 ~35% No 31 California 1060 533 527 ~30% No 32 Maryland 1055 530 525 ~35% No 33 Georgia 1050 528 522 ~45% No 34 Texas 1045 525 520 ~40% No 35 Washington 1040 523 517 ~35% No 36 Nevada 1035 520 515 ~25% No 37 South Carolina 1030 518 512 ~50% No 38 Maine 1020 513 507 ~65% No 39 Indiana 1010 508 502 ~70% Yes 40 Florida 1005 505 500 ~60% No 41 Ohio 1000 503 497 ~55% No 42 Illinois 995 500 495 ~70% No 43 Rhode Island 985 495 490 ~75% Yes 44 Michigan 975 490 485 ~85% Yes 45 Connecticut 970 488 482 ~90% Yes 46 Colorado 960 483 477 ~95% Yes 47 District of Columbia 950 478 472 ~80% No 48 Idaho 945 475 470 ~85% No 49 Delaware 933 470 463 ~94% Yes 50 West Virginia 911 459 452 ~93% Yes 51 New Mexico 875 441 434 ~100% Yes Source: Data compiled from the College Board 2025 Annual Report and state-level reporting. ERW and Math breakdowns for some states are estimated from total scores where individual section data was not separately published. Rankings reflect the Class of 2025. The pattern is impossible to miss. Every state in the top 10 has a participation rate under 5%. Every state in the bottom 10 has participation above 85%. This is the single most important fact about average SAT scores by state, and most rankings pages bury it in a footnote. Key Takeaways From the 2026 State Rankings Finding What It Means Highest state average: Kansas (1256) Extremely low participation inflates scores Lowest state average: New Mexico (875) Universal testing lowers averages Top 10 states Every state has participation below 5% Bottom 10 states Most states have participation above 85% National average 1029 Best admissions benchmark Your target college's middle 50% SAT range The most important conclusion is simple: participation rate predicts SAT averages better than educational quality. Why State SAT Averages Vary So Much The Participation Rate Effect The gap between the highest and lowest state averages is roughly 379 points. That sounds enormous until you understand its cause. Research shows that a 10 percentage point increase in SAT participation correlates with a 21 to 23 point decrease in a state’s average score. This single variable explains over 70 to 80% of the variance between states. The logic is straightforward. In Kansas (participation around 2%), only students actively pursuing competitive college admissions bother to take the SAT. These are typically the highest-performing students in any school. In New Mexico (participation at 100%), every eleventh grader sits for the exam, including students who have no plans for college and students with significant academic challenges. SAT-Mandate States vs. ACT-Dominant States Nine states currently use the SAT as their statewide accountability assessment for high schoolers: Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Indiana, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Rhode Island, and West Virginia. Starting in 2026, Kentucky will switch from requiring the ACT to requiring the SAT. Meanwhile, roughly 16 states (concentrated in the Midwest and South) use the ACT as their default test. In those states, the few students who also take the SAT are almost always high achievers targeting schools on the coasts. This self-selection pushes SAT averages artificially high in ACT-dominant territory. If you’re in an ACT-dominant state weighing whether to take the SAT instead, our ACT prep resources can help you compare readiness across both tests. State Participation Average Score New Mexico 100% 875 Colorado 95% 960 Connecticut 90% 970 Michigan 85% 975 Delaware 94% 933 Self-Selection Bias The College Board itself has been explicit about this problem. The Board states: “Since the population of test-takers is self-selected, using aggregate SAT scores to compare or evaluate schools, districts, states or other educational units is not valid.” That quote deserves more attention than it gets. It means the very rankings that fill the top of Google results, including the table above, are not measuring what most people assume they measure. Other Contributing Factors Participation rate is the dominant variable, but it’s not the only one. School funding levels, household income distribution, the proportion of English language learners, and access to test preparation all play secondary roles. These factors matter more when comparing states with similar participation rates, such as Connecticut (around 90%) and Colorado (around 95%), where differences in educational investment can show through. States with the Highest Average SAT Scores Kansas (1256), North Dakota (1254), Wyoming (1253), Utah (1230), and Nebraska (1228) top the raw rankings. All of these states have participation rates between 1% and 2%. These are not the “best” states for education. They are the most self-selected. When only 1 in 50 students takes the SAT, you are measuring the performance of a tiny, highly motivated subset. Participation-Adjusted Rankings Tell a Different Story PrepScholar published a participation-adjusted ranking using statistical normalization, and the results flip the conventional wisdom. When you control for participation rate, Massachusetts and Connecticut emerge as the top-performing states. Both have relatively large education budgets, some of the strongest school systems in the country, and high concentrations of college-oriented families. At the other end, Alabama and West Virginia rank lowest on a participation-adjusted basis. This adjusted view is far more meaningful for anyone trying to genuinely assess educational quality across states. The raw rankings are, bluntly, misleading. States with the Lowest Average SAT Scores New Mexico (875 with 100% participation), West Virginia (911 with 93%), and Delaware (933 with 94%) sit at the bottom of the raw rankings. These states are not failing. They are testing every student. A student scoring 1050 in New Mexico is performing well above that state’s average and competing with a far tougher curve than someone scoring 1250 in Wyoming, where only the top 1% of students opt in. Practitioners in online tutoring communities note that parents frequently misread these numbers. As one analysis observed , a parent in North Dakota might see 1254 and assume their child is already ahead, while a parent in New Mexico might see 875 and panic that their state is failing. Neither reaction reflects what the data actually shows, and both can lead to poor decisions about test preparation. If you’re in a mandatory-testing state and want to build a targeted study plan, working through SAT practice questions organized by skill and difficulty level is more useful than stressing about your state’s raw average. How to Read Your State’s Average (What It Actually Means for You) State averages are context, not targets. Here’s a three-step framework for making them useful: Step 1: Check Your State’s Participation Rate Find your state in the table above. If participation is above 50%, the average includes many students who aren’t actively preparing for college admissions. Your state’s average will look low compared to low-participation states, but that says nothing about you personally. Step 2: Compare Your Score to National Percentiles National percentiles are a much better yardstick than state averages. Here’s where key scores fall: SAT Score National Percentile 1500 98th 1400 93rd 1300 86th 1200 76th 1100 63rd 1000 48th A 1200 puts you above roughly three-quarters of all test-takers nationwide, regardless of which state you live in. Step 3: Look Up Your Target College’s Middle 50% Range The benchmark that actually matters for admissions is the middle 50% SAT range published in each school’s Common Data Set. This is the 25th-to-75th percentile band of enrolled students (not applicants). If a school’s middle 50% is 1350 to 1500, aim for at least 1350, ideally higher. That number is your real target, not the average for your state. Using a score predictor based on your diagnostic performance can help you gauge how much work stands between your current level and your target school’s range. Average SAT Score by State vs. National Percentiles Many students assume a state average can be converted directly into a percentile. Unfortunately, it doesn't work that way. A student earning a 1200 in Colorado and a student earning a 1200 in Wyoming have exactly the same SAT score, but they're being compared against very different groups of test-takers. Use national percentiles instead of state averages. SAT Score National Percentile 1500 98th 1400 93rd 1300 86th 1200 76th 1100 63rd 1000 48th National percentiles eliminate participation bias and provide a standardized way to compare scores across all 50 states. SAT Score Benchmarks: What Counts as “Good”? “Good” depends entirely on where you’re applying. Here’s a rough framework by school tier: Most public universities: 1100 to 1300 Competitive state universities and selective privates: 1200 to 1400 Ivy League and top-tier schools: 1450 to 1600 For scholarship purposes, scores of 1200 to 1300 often unlock regional merit aid at state universities. Scores above 1500 can qualify for partial or full scholarships at highly selective institutions. The College Board’s own college readiness benchmarks (480 RW and 530 Math, totaling 1010) represent a floor, not a competitive target. They indicate a student is likely prepared for introductory college coursework, nothing more. If you’re looking to close the gap between where you are now and where you need to be, a structured approach helps. Our guide on how to improve your SAT score by 200 points breaks down the process into concrete steps. Why State Averages Matter More in 2026 The Return of Test-Required Admissions The test-optional wave that swept higher education during the pandemic is receding. A growing list of selective colleges has reinstated standardized test requirements, including MIT, Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown, Dartmouth, Cornell, Caltech, and the University of Texas at Austin. Six of the eight Ivy League universities now mandate SAT or ACT scores for Fall 2026 admissions. This means more students need to take the SAT seriously, and state-level context matters for understanding how your peers are performing and what preparation looks like in your area. The Testing Map Is Shifting Kentucky’s switch from an ACT mandate to an SAT mandate in 2026 will add tens of thousands of new test-takers to the SAT pool. Expect Kentucky’s average to drop sharply from its current 1198 (at roughly 4% participation) once every student is required to test. This is not a decline in educational quality. It’s a change in who gets counted. The Digital SAT Baseline With 97% of the Class of 2025 taking the Digital SAT, the 2025 data represents the first clean, nearly-all-digital baseline. Future year-over-year comparisons will be much more reliable now that the transition from paper to digital is essentially complete. Students preparing for the Digital SAT should focus on the format’s specific features, including the adaptive testing structure and built-in Desmos calculator. SAT vs. ACT: The Geographic Split Understanding average SAT scores by state also requires knowing which test dominates in each region. Coastal states (especially in the Northeast and parts of the West Coast) lean heavily toward the SAT. The Midwest and much of the South default to the ACT. This geographic split is why you’ll see states like Iowa or Montana with SAT participation under 3% but ACT participation above 60%. It doesn’t mean students in those states aren’t testing. They’re just testing with a different exam. For students in ACT-dominant states who are curious about the SAT, or vice versa, taking a diagnostic on both can clarify which test better suits your strengths. A study schedule guide can help you plan once you’ve chosen your test. How to Find Out Whether Your State Requires the SAT If your state's average score seems unusually high or low, the first thing to check is whether the SAT is mandatory. Ask these questions: Does my state require all students to take the SAT? Is my state primarily an ACT state? What percentage of students in my state take the SAT? Is the SAT used as an accountability assessment? States that require the SAT typically report lower averages because every student participates. States dominated by the ACT often report much higher SAT averages because only a small group of college-bound students choose to take the exam. Frequently Asked Questions What is a good SAT score compared to my state average? It depends on your state’s participation rate. If you’re in a high-participation state like Connecticut or Colorado, beating your state average by even 100 points is significant. In a low-participation state like Wyoming, the state average is inflated by self-selection. Compare yourself to national percentiles instead: 1200 is the 76th percentile, and 1300 is the 86th percentile nationwide. Why does my state have such a low average SAT score? Almost certainly because your state requires all students to take the SAT. Mandatory testing includes every student regardless of college plans, academic preparation, or language background. This drives the average down compared to states where only self-selected, college-bound students sit for the exam. Is 1200 a good SAT score? Yes. A 1200 places you at approximately the 76th percentile nationally, meaning you scored higher than roughly three out of four test-takers. It’s competitive for most public universities and puts you in range for many selective schools, though highly competitive institutions typically look for 1400 or above. Should I compare my score to my state average or the national average? Neither is your most useful benchmark. The national average (1029) and your state average are useful for general context, but your real target should be the middle 50% range of the colleges you’re applying to. That range, found in each school’s Common Data Set, tells you exactly where admitted students score. How is the SAT scored? The SAT is scored on a scale of 400 to 1600. It consists of two sections: Reading and Writing (200 to 800) and Math (200 to 800). The scores from both sections are added together for your total. There is no penalty for guessing. Which states require the SAT? As of 2025, the states using the SAT as a statewide assessment include Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Indiana, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Rhode Island, and West Virginia. Kentucky will join this list in 2026, switching from an ACT mandate. Has the average SAT score been going up or down? After several years of post-pandemic decline, the national average ticked up slightly from 1024 (Class of 2024) to 1029 (Class of 2025). But scores remain well below the pre-pandemic average of around 1060. The 2025 data is the first year where nearly all students took the Digital SAT, making it a cleaner baseline for tracking future trends. What should I actually do with this state-by-state data? Use it for context, not as a goal. Understand your state’s participation rate so you can interpret the average correctly. Then focus on the numbers that matter for your admissions strategy: national percentiles and your target schools’ middle 50% ranges. From there, build a prep plan that closes the specific gap between your current score and your target. Ready to find out where you stand? Take a free SAT practice exam to get a realistic baseline score and build your study plan from there.

title: Sony Electronics Launches FE 100-400mm F5.6-8 OSS: The Perfect Hobbyist’s Super-Telephoto Zoom Lens
summary: The new lens delivers outstanding mobility and excellent image quality across the entire zoom range.
body_text: San Diego, August 4, 2026 - Sony Electronics introduces SEL100400 - FE 100-400mm F5.6-8 OSS , a super-telephoto zoom lens for 35mm full-frame Alpha™ E-mount cameras. Despite its super-telephoto reach of up to 400mm, the lens stays compact and lightweight, weighing just 654g (approx.). Its latest optical design incorporates two ED (Extra-low Dispersion) glass elements and two aspherical elements, delivering excellent image quality and clear rendering across the entire zoom range no matter how far away the subject is. The lens also features fast, precise AF (autofocus) and built-in optical image stabilization to support handheld shooting, letting you quickly capture moving subjects such as birds, sports, trains, and aircraft. “With the needs of a large set of hobbyist photographers in mind, from birders to parents, we used our expertise in professional lens technology to create a high-quality, affordable super-telephoto zoom lens that will go the distance,” said Yang Cheng, Vice President of Imaging Solutions, Sony Electronics. Pricing & Availability: The SEL100400 - FE 100-400MM F5.6-8 OSS will be available for a suggested retail price of $849.99 USD / $1,079.99 CAD from September 2026. Key Features Of The FE 100-400mm F/5.6-8 OSS: Compact, Lightweight Design For Easy Handling, Even For First-Time Super-Telephoto Users The lens delivers a 100-400mm super-telephoto zoom range in a compact, lightweight body weighing approximately 654g, making it easy to carry. That portability also eases handling during handheld shooting and speeds up framing. You can capture powerful images of subjects that are hard to approach, such as birds and sports scenes, and use the ‘compression effect’ (which makes the distance between nearby subjects and distant background elements appear shorter) for landscape work unique to super-telephoto lenses. With an optional SEL20TC teleconverter1, you can double your reach, up to 800mm, or up to 1,200mm in APS-C mode. Sharp Detail Through The Entire Zoom Range Means You Can Capture The Details That Matter Excellent image quality holds whatever the shooting distance, thanks to an optical design with two ED glass elements and two aspherical elements that suppress color bleeding and distortion for clear rendering across the entire zoom range. The subject stands out against natural, soft bokeh, helped by a 9-blade circular aperture and optimization of spherical aberration. Its close-up performance is strong too: a minimum focusing distance of 0.86 m at the telephoto end and 1.13 m at the wide end, with a maximum magnification of 0.41x, lets you shoot flowers, insects, and other nearby subjects as easily as distant ones. Fast, Precise AF and Built-In Optical Image Stabilization For Moving Subjects The linear motor drive delivers fast, precise, and quiet AF (auto focus) to track moving subjects. The lens also supports high-speed continuous shooting with AF/AE (auto exposure) tracking at up to approximately 120 frames per second2 with the full-frame mirrorless Alpha 9 III camera. Built-in optical image stabilization suppresses camera shake during handheld shooting and keeps framing stable, even with distant subjects. The lens also works with the camera body’s Active Mode image stabilization and coordinated image stabilization control3, for high-quality stills and movies with reduced blur when shooting handheld. It also supports the camera body’s breathing compensation function4, which corrects changes in angle of view caused by shifts in focus position during movie recording. Usability & Reliability Built For Outdoor Adventures With Dust & Moisture Resistance A customizable focus hold button, focus mode/range switching dial, and zoom lock switch give you quick operation across shooting scenes and comfortable ultra-telephoto handling. A dust and moisture resistant design5 helps you keep shooting with confidence when the weather changes unexpectedly. The supplied lens hood helps prevent flare and ghosting that can degrade image quality. Check out a product video for the new FE 100-400MM F5.6-8 OSS here . For more information, visit: https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel100400 Notes 1When the 2x teleconverter ‘SEL20TC’ is attached. Sold separately. 2Based on Sony test conditions. Continuous shooting speed may decrease depending on shooting conditions. When focus mode is set to AF-C, continuous shooting speed varies depending on the lens attached. Please check the lens compatibility information support page for details. 3Please refer to support information for compatible cameras. 4Please refer to support information for compatible cameras. When this function is set to [On], angle of view and image quality may change slightly. Depending on the lens, compensation may not be fully effective even when this function is set to [On]. 5Not guaranteed to be 100% dust and moisture resistant. About Sony Electronics Inc. Sony Electronics is a subsidiary of Sony Corporation of America and an affiliate of Sony Group Corporation, one of the most comprehensive entertainment companies in the world, with a portfolio that encompasses electronics, music, motion pictures, mobile, gaming, robotics and financial services. Headquartered in San Diego, California, Sony Electronics is a leader in electronics for the consumer and professional markets. Operations include research and development, engineering, sales, marketing, distribution and customer service. Sony Electronics creates products that innovate and inspire generations, such as the award-winning Alpha Interchangeable Lens Cameras and revolutionary high-resolution audio products.

body_text: If you want to send money to Nigeria using stablecoins, you can get dollars to loved ones in minutes instead of days, often for less. Take Ngozi, a data analyst in Dallas, Texas, who sends part of her paycheck home monthly. Her parents live in Enugu. For years, she used her bank’s international wire service. She watched days pass before the money arrived. The fees and exchange-rate markdowns also frustrated her. They quietly reduced what her parents actually received. A friend eventually showed her how to send money to Nigeria using stablecoins instead, and her whole routine changed. Now the transfer clears before she is done making dinner, and her parents see the exact amount she sent. Stories like Ngozi’s are becoming the norm rather than the exception. More people abroad are learning to send money to Nigeria using stablecoins. The process is faster, cheaper, and easier to track than traditional remittance channels. Why people in the U.S. send money to Nigeria Using stablecoins Nigeria is one of the largest crypto and stablecoin markets in the world. According to the International Monetary Fund , Nigeria received close to $59 billion in crypto-asset inflows in a single year, with stablecoins forming a major share of that volume. Nigeria alone accounts for roughly 60% of all stablecoin inflows into Sub-Saharan Africa since 2019. The reason is simple economics. World Bank data shows that sending $200 to Sub-Saharan Africa through conventional channels costs close to 9% on average, well above the 6% global average and far above the 3% target world leaders set for 2030. Bank wires can take three to five business days to clear. Exchange-rate markups can also reduce the amount the recipient receives. People are paying more than they should for money transfers to Nigeria. That’s why many now use stablecoins instead of relying only on banks. What are stablecoins? Stablecoins are digital tokens designed to hold a steady value, usually pegged one-to-one with the US dollar. Unlike other digital assets that can swing wildly in price within a single day, a stablecoin is built to stay stable. This explains the name. That stability makes stablecoins practical for sending money to Nigeria. You don’t have to worry as much about the value changing before it arrives. title: HAL strengthens partnership for Prachand light combat helicopter production
summary: Adani Defence Systems and Technologies Limited and Bharat Earth Movers Limited intend to manufacture fuselage structures for the aircraft.
body_text: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) has entered into partnerships with the Indian industry— Adani Defence Systems and Technologies Limited and Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML)—for manufacturing fuselage structures for the Prachand light combat helicopter (LCH), further expanding India’s indigenous helicopter production ecosystem. Under the agreements, BEML and Adani Defence will manufacture 48 and 42 fuselage structures, respectively. Shri Tushar Ranjan Behera, general manager, Helicopter Division, signed the agreement with Cmde (Retd.) R. G. K. Rao, ED, Aerospace & Maritime for BEML and Shri Prasanna Karthik, vice president, ADSTL, for Adani Defence in the presence of the senior leadership of HAL, BEML and ADSTL. “This partnership marks a significant step in strengthening India’s aerospace ecosystem. For the first time, the private industry is being integrated into the production of helicopter fuselage structures. This partnership will expand capacity, strengthen the domestic supply chain and contribute to enhancing indigenous aerospace manufacturing capabilities,” said Shri Ravi K, CMD, HAL. HAL has augmented the capacity and already commenced production of the 156 Prachand LCHs ordered for the Indian Armed Forces at its new helicopter manufacturing facility in Tumakuru, Karnataka. The establishment of two additional production lines will further enhance overall manufacturing capability for the LCH program and support the timely delivery of the helicopters to the Indian Armed Forces. The expanded industrial base is also expected to create opportunities for a wider network of Indian MSMEs, component manufacturers and aerospace suppliers, contributing to the development of specialized capabilities and strengthening the domestic aerospace supply chain. This press release was prepared and distributed by HAL.

title: Chevron Strengthens North American Base Oils Distribution Network
summary: HOUSTON --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 3, 2026-- Chevron Products Company, a division of Chevron U.S.A. Inc., will expand its North American base oils distribution network, strengthening customer access to premium base oils and process oils through complementary distribution agreements with HF Sinclair
body_text: Press Release < Back View Printer friendly Version 08/03/26 Chevron Strengthens North American Base Oils Distribution Network HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 3, 2026-- Chevron Products Company, a division of Chevron U.S.A. Inc., will expand its North American base oils distribution network, strengthening customer access to premium base oils and process oils through complementary distribution agreements with HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties and Renkert Oil . Effective May 1, 2027, HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties will become Chevron's exclusive distributor of Group II base oils in Canada, and its existing customer territories in the U.S. HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties will also have non-exclusive distribution rights for Group II base oils in select additional regions of the U.S. Renkert Oil will continue as Chevron's distributor for Paralux® and Paramount™ process oils throughout the United States, Canada and Europe; NEXBASE® Group III base oils in the United States and Canada; and Chevron Group II base oils throughout the United States outside HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties’ exclusive territory. Together, the two distributors expand Chevron's customer reach through a complementary set of regional and product-focused channels. Customers will benefit from dependable supply, local inventory, responsive technical support and access to one of the industry's premium base oil portfolios. "Customers need more than high-quality products – they need confidence in their supply partner," said Alicia Logan, general manager, Chevron Base Oils. "By working with both HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties and Renkert Oil, we're building on each partner's unique strengths to deliver reliable supply, local expertise and the flexibility our customers need as markets continue to evolve." HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties segment, which announced on July 28 the decision to retire its base oil refining assets in Mississauga, Ontario, brings an established logistics network, regional infrastructure and strong customer relationships that enhance Chevron's ability to serve customers across Canada and throughout its expanded U.S. distribution footprint. Renkert Oil has decades of experience serving process oil customers and lubricant manufacturers and will continue to deliver the technical expertise, reliable logistics and responsive support customers expect. "Together, HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties and Renkert Oil provide complementary capabilities that strengthen our distribution network while ensuring customers continue to receive the products, service and technical expertise they expect from Chevron," Logan said. Chevron is one of the world's leading suppliers of premium Group II, Group II+, and Group III base oils. With the introduction of Group III+ in early 2027, Chevron will offer one of the industry's most comprehensive premium base oil portfolios, supported by extensive OEM and additive qualifications, world-class technical expertise and a resilient global manufacturing network. By leveraging the strengths of HF Sinclair Lubricants & Specialties and Renkert Oil, Chevron is reinforcing its long-term commitment to customer success through expanded market coverage, resilient supply and specialized distribution channels designed to meet the evolving needs of lubricant manufacturers and process oil customers. About Chevron Base Oils Worldwide, Chevron Base Oils is one of the largest producers of premium Group II and Group III base oils. We offer a global slate of products having the same specifications produced at five manufacturing facilities and distributed through 20 hubs globally. Lubricant marketers produce a broad range of products from automotive engine oils to driveline fluids, industrial oils to turbine oils. As a full line premium base oil producer, Chevron helps lubricant marketers optimize formulations across their increasingly complex product portfolio. Information on Chevron’s base oil business can be found at chevronbaseoils.com . About HF Sinclair Corporation HF Sinclair Corporation, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, is an independent energy company that produces and markets high-value light products such as gasoline, diesel fuel, jet fuel, renewable diesel and other specialty products. HF Sinclair owns and operates refineries in Kansas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, Washington and Utah. HF Sinclair provides petroleum products and crude oil transportation, terminaling, storage and throughput services to its refineries and the petroleum industry. HF Sinclair markets its refined products principally in the Southwest U.S., the Rocky Mountains extending into the Pacific Northwest and in other neighboring Plains states. It supplies high-quality fuels to more than 1,800 branded stations and licenses the use of the Sinclair brand to more than 350 additional locations throughout the country. HF Sinclair produces renewable diesel at two of its facilities in Wyoming and also at its facility in Artesia, New Mexico. In addition, we produce and market base oils and other specialized lubricants in the U.S., Canada and the Netherlands, and export products to more than 80 countries. About Renkert Oil Renkert Oil LLC, founded in 1987, is a Chevron base oil and process oil distributor in North America, as well as an independent manufacturer of specialty products. In addition to premium products, Renkert Oil also provides technical services and consulting for niche industry oil applications. View source version on businesswire.com: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260803871542/en/ Ross Allen ross.allen@chevron.com Source: Chevron Corporation
